sections.h2: What does the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds do?
sections.html:
Corunna's courthouse holds the land records for every parcel in the county. Incoming papers are checked against the state recording act, numbered, timed and indexed, and the originals are stored for safekeeping. A question about who owns a given parcel gets answered from this office's books.

Michigan's 1835 constitution created the recording office in each county. Shiawassee's books start in 1836, a year before the county itself was organized. From 1954 on, records are scanned into the computer system, and all of it can be searched by liber and page. The address is the Circuit Courthouse, 208 N. Shiawassee Street, first floor, Corunna, MI 48817. Phone 989-743-2216 or write rod@shiawassee.net.

The county's boundaries were first drawn in 1822, carved out of Oakland and St. Clair counties and named for the Shiawassee River. For years it was attached to neighboring counties for revenue and court matters. Only after Michigan became a state in 1837 did the state authorize a county government of its own.

sections.h2: When is the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds open?
sections.html:
The counter is staffed on weekdays, 8:00 a.m. until noon, then 1:05 p.m. until 5:00 p.m. The search room closes a little earlier in each half of the day. Because a county holiday page asks visitors to phone and book an appointment, call ahead before carrying in a closing package.

Recording is paid in cash or by check made out to the Register of Deeds. Card payment covers copies and searches, with a $1.00 convenience fee when you print from the website.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to record a deed in Shiawassee County?
sections.html:
Recording one instrument costs $30.00. A deed that carries a warranty clause also needs a $5.00 tax certificate under MCL 211.135. The treasurer issues it from the second floor of the courthouse (989-743-2224). Land contracts, their assignments and condominium master deeds need the same certificate.

sections.h2: How does the Michigan transfer tax work in Shiawassee County?
sections.html:
Recording a sale deed triggers a county tax under MCL 207.505 and a state tax under MCL 207.526. Shiawassee's schedule gives multipliers of .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county and tabulates the amounts in $500 bands. The first band, $100.00 up to $500, shows $3.75 state and $0.55 county.

  • The seller, as grantor, pays.
  • The deed face shows total consideration and any claimed exemption.
  • A parcel crossing a county line splits the price between the two counties.
  • Stamps can be bought only in the county where the land lies.
  • Filing a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit costs nothing if the deed refers to it.

sections.h2: Which transfers are exempt from the transfer tax?
sections.html: The exemption excerpt on the county site covers, among others, consideration under $100, security instruments, leases, and spousal deeds that create or end a tenancy by the entireties. Family transfers often rely on the exemptions for a corrective quitclaim and for a new joint tenancy where one joint owner already held title. Ask the staff which subsection to cite on the deed.

sections.h2: What makes a Shiawassee County deed recordable?
sections.html:
The office posts a piece of Act 103 of 1937 (MCL 565.201) with its acceptance tests. Staff need the original paper with original signatures, a typed name under each signature, the grantee's address, a 2.5 inch blank band at the top of page one, and the drafter's name and address. The first five digits of any Social Security number must be removed.

A deed of unplatted land must also repeat the right-to-farm statement from MCL 560.109, warning that nearby farms may produce noise, dust and odors, which matters in a county where 59.8 percent of residents lived in rural areas in 2020. When a spouse dies, the survivor brings a certified death certificate. No replacement deed is issued, since the office only records.

sections.h2: What else does Shiawassee County list for sellers and buyers?
sections.html:
Sheriff's sales are held Wednesday mornings at 10:00 a.m. in the 35th Circuit Court lobby, and bidders need a certified check for the full opening bid. The office also links a property fraud alert service. Michigan leaves assessing and zoning to cities and townships, and the County Equalization department (989-743-2263) works across the county's 21 units of local government, fielding questions on valuation, millage and exemption status.

The county covers 541 square miles. The Shiawassee River passes through Corunna, the county seat, and Owosso, the largest city. Durand, Laingsburg, Perry and part of Ovid are the other cities. I-69 enters near the southwest corner and leaves east of Durand, where Amtrak's Blue Water train stops, and M-21 serves Corunna and Owosso. The 2010 population center of Michigan fell in Bennington Township.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Shiawassee County housing?
sections.html:
The 2025 estimate is 67,681 residents, against 70,648 in 2010. The 2020 census found a median age of 43.3, with 19.8 percent of residents 65 or older, and 27,889 households. Of 30,231 housing units that year, 7.7 percent were vacant. For 2020 through 2024, the Census Bureau counts 28,126 households and says owners occupy 80.1 percent of homes. Only 71 building permits were issued in 2025.

The median value for a home lived in by its owner is $171,600. Median rent is $899, and median household income is $67,404. At 128 people per square mile and a 27.8 minute average commute, most parcels sit outside a city street grid.

The local economy is small and spread out. The Census Bureau counted 1,202 employer establishments in 2023 with 14,259 jobs and a payroll of about $655 million, and 4,579 businesses with no employees in 2024. Retail sales reached roughly $1.18 billion in 2022. Residents are settled: 92.3 percent lived in the same house a year earlier, and 92.7 percent of adults finished high school. For a seller, that means fewer people moving in from elsewhere, and buyers who know the area well.

sections.h2: Which other county pages help a Shiawassee seller?
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds site links several pages worth reading before a closing. They include a property fraud alert signup, the sheriff sale information page, the county transfer tax exemption excerpt, the state exemption form and a link to the Michigan Homeowner Assistance Fund program at MSHDA. Owners who are behind on a mortgage can start with that last link before deciding to sell.

The county treasurer collects and distributes tax roll levies for schools, townships, cities and villages, and its site includes a page for paying delinquent taxes online. Ask the treasurer for the balance on your parcel before you sign a purchase agreement, since the tax certificate on a warranty deed depends on those taxes being current.

faqs.q: What does recording cost at the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Recording is $30.00 per document. Warranty deeds and land contracts also need a $5.00 treasurer's tax certificate, and the transfer taxes follow the sale price.

faqs.q: Which party owes transfer tax on a Shiawassee County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. The county's schedule says the tax falls on the seller or grantor, using .0075 for the state and .0011 for the county.

faqs.q: Can a photocopy of a deed be recorded in Shiawassee County?
faqs.a: No. The office wants the original with original signatures. After recording, a copy is $1.00 a page, or $5.00 more certified.

faqs.q: Does a spouse's death produce a new deed in Shiawassee County?
faqs.a: No. Bring a certified death certificate and the recording fee, and the office shows the deceased owner holds no further interest. The existing deed stays in force.

faqs.q: Where is the Shiawassee County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: On the first floor of the Circuit Courthouse, 208 N. Shiawassee Street, Corunna, MI 48817. Call 989-743-2216 first, since the holiday page asks visitors to book an appointment.
